logp.method_description: The n-octanol/water partition coefficient of compounds 4a,b and 5a,b was determined using the shake-flask method. Phosphate buffer solution (PBS), doubly distilled water [100 mL, phosphate buffer, (PO43–) = 10 mM, (NaCl) = 15 m, pH adjusted to 7.4 with hydrochloric acid] and n-octanol (100 mL) were shaken together using a laboratory shaker (IKA KS 130 basic) for 72 h to allow saturation of both phases. Then, a stock solution of each compound (50 μL) in n-octanol was mixed with n-octanol (700 μL) and buffer (750 μL) for 10 min with a laboratory vortexer (VWR Analogue Vortexer). The resultant emulsion was centrifuged (3000 g, 5 min) to separate the phases. A 500 μL aliquot of each phase was taken and diluted to 1000 μL with the appropriate phase. The concentration of each complex in the aqueous and organic phase was determined with an Agilent 8453 UV/Vis diode array spectrophotometer at 280 nm. The value of log D7.4 is defined as the logarithm of the ratio of the concentration of the complex in the organic and aqueous phase (log D7.4 = log {[complex(org)]/[complex(aq.)]}). The values reported are the mean of three separate determinations.
